summary: I sent the bounded brief with no visual cues. The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, read the settings files, and then on its own started the visual companion with start-server.sh. It wrote a layout.html screen comparing three layouts (A stacked, B two-column, C sidebar tabs), gave me a localhost URL, and asked me to pick. I replied with option A, and it updated settings.html and settings.css. It wrote no spec or plan file.
reasoning: All 8 criteria were met, and I checked each against the session log and the files on disk. The agent decided by itself that a layout question was worth showing visually and started the companion only once that question came up. It kept the design in chat with no spec or plan file, got my approval, and then implemented the change.

observations.description: The agent said "I've opened the three layout options in a browser tab". It only started a server and gave me a URL; it didn't open a tab. The wording is a little misleading.

The agent picked the field groupings (Profile, Preferences, Notifications, Security) itself and didn't ask a clarifying question about them. It did invite changes ("tell me if you'd group any fields differently"). That's reasonable for a bounded task.

Mockups were written into the project's .hyperpowers/ folder. The repo has no .gitignore, so the folder shows up as untracked. The agent pointed this out and offered to add .gitignore. The skill could default to a location outside the repo, or add the ignore entry automatically.
Claude Code first-run trust and bypass-permission dialogs default to "No, exit". I had to press Down to accept them. This is harness/onboarding noise, not the product under test.
The agent stopped the companion server and wrote a waiting.html screen once implementation began. That is a tidy cleanup.

criteria.evidence: Session log: the first tool call is Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}, before any Edit to public/*. Agent text: "Using brainstorming to shape the settings layout rework."

criteria.criterion: Visual companion opened: start-server.sh run, localhost URL given, HTML screen with candidate layouts written
criteria.evidence: Log shows Bash running `.../skills/brainstorming/scripts/start-server.sh --project-dir ...`, then a Write to .hyperpowers/brainstorm/52538-1790841723/content/layout.html. The screen showed "http://localhost:54117/?key=639e11f3...". grep of layout.html found headings "A. Stacked sections", "B. Two-column sections" and "C. Sidebar tabs", plus 3 data-choice elements.

criteria.criterion: Opened just-in-time, not upfront; no non-visual questions routed through browser
criteria.evidence: Log order: Skill, git ls-files, cat the settings files, read visual-companion.md, start-server.sh, write layout.html. The agent read the code before starting the server. The only screen it wrote was layout.html, which asks "How should the grouped settings page be laid out?". It asked no scope questions in the browser. Its message said "tell me if you'd group any fields differently" in the terminal, and the proposed grouping was listed in the terminal as well.

criteria.criterion: Bounded classification held; companion did not escalate ceremony
criteria.evidence: The design stayed in chat: one terminal message with the proposed groups, options A/B/C and a recommendation, then implementation right after my pick. Only one Skill call appears in the log (hyperpowers:brainstorming). It did not invoke a spec or plan step.
`ls docs` returned "No such file or directory". `find . -type f` (excluding .git) lists only .hyperpowers/brainstorm/* mockups, README.md, public/*, package.json and src/*.

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: jq filter for Skill tool_use returned only {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}. The find output shows no plan file.

criteria.criterion: Asked approval of layout before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Before any edit to public/ files it asked: "Which layout do you want? You can click one in the browser or reply here." The edits to public/settings.html and settings.css appear in the log only after my reply.

Agent text: "Implementing option A: `settings.html` and `settings.css` only". The log shows Edit calls to public/settings.html and public/settings.css. `git status` shows "M public/settings.css" and "M public/settings.html".
